title: A constructible abelian sheaf on a quasi-compact scheme is killed by a positive integer
statement: Let $T$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $C$ a constructible abelian sheaf on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf]. Then there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $n\cdot\mathrm{id}_C=0$ in $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]; in particular every stalk $C_{\bar t}$ at a geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a finite abelian group killed by $n$. (Ingredients: each stratum $T_k$ is constructible, hence retrocompact (Stacks Topology 09YH), hence quasi-compact as $T$ is; $Z_k$ is homeomorphic to $T_k$, so finitely many members $V_1,\dots,V_s$ of the trivializing etale covering of $\iota_k^{-1}C$ already cover $Z_k$, etale maps being open; with $n$ the least common multiple of the orders $|A_i|$ over all strata and these finitely many $i$, $n$ kills each $\underline{A_i}$, hence each $\iota_k^{-1}C$ (a sheaf whose restrictions to a covering are killed by $n$ is killed by $n$), hence every geometric stalk of $C$ (the stalk of $C$ at a geometric point of $T_k$ is the stalk of $\iota_k^{-1}C$ at its lift to $Z_k$), hence $C$, a map of abelian sheaves vanishing on all geometric stalks being zero. Stacks uses this without statement, e.g. in Lemma 09YT and Theorem 03SC.)
